english: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, with $\cot^{-1}$ taking values in $(0,\pi)$, let $S$ be the set of all integers $n$ with $1\le|n|\le10$ such that $\cot^{-1}(\cot n)=\tan^{-1}(\tan n)$. Then the sum of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: प्रतिलोम त्रिकोणमितीय फलनों के केवल मुख्य मानों को लेते हुए, जहाँ $\cot^{-1}$ के मान $(0,\pi)$ में हैं, माना कि $S$ उन सभी पूर्णांकों $n$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $1\le|n|\le10$ तथा $\cot^{-1}(\cot n)=\tan^{-1}(\tan n)$ है। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग ______ है।
solution: Both sides differ from $n$ by a multiple of $\pi$; $\cot^{-1}(\cot n)=r\in(0,\pi)$ where $r=n-\pi\left[\dfrac{n}{\pi}\right]$
$\tan^{-1}(\tan n)=r$ if $r<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $r-\pi$ if $r>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so equality $\iff r\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
solution_full: Let $r$ be the number in $(0,\pi)$ with $n-r$ a multiple of $\pi$; since $\pi$ is irrational, $n$ is never a multiple of $\pi$, so $\cot n$ and $\tan n$ are defined and $r\neq\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
$\cot^{-1}(\cot n)$ is the angle in $(0,\pi)$ with the same cotangent as $n$; since $\cot$ has period $\pi$, it equals $r$.

$\tan^{-1}(\tan n)$ is the angle in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ congruent to $n$ modulo $\pi$: it is $r$ when $r<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $r-\pi$ when $r>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. So the two sides are equal exactly when $0<r<\dfrac{\pi}{2}\approx1.571$.
originality_note: New: equality of cot^-1(cot n) and tan^-1(tan n) at integer points holds exactly when n mod pi is in (0, pi/2); because the two principal ranges are not symmetric, n and -n behave oppositely and the sum over 1 <= |n| <= 10 is not zero (way 4). Closest known: evaluating tan^-1(tan 10) or cot^-1(cot(-11)) individually. Different because: the question is about a set of integers defined by comparing two principal ranges, and the asymmetry gives the answer.

concept_use.Properties of Inverse trigonometric func: cot^-1(cot x) = x - k pi in (0,pi) and tan^-1(tan x) = x - k pi in (-pi/2, pi/2) are used to decide equality for each integer.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, principal values are stated, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with mpmath/numpy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that n = 0 is excluded (cot 0 undefined) by 1 <= |n|, that no integer is near a boundary where rounding could mislead (closest is r(-3) = 0.142, far from 0 and pi/2), and that -11 is a negative integer. Changed: No change.
key_step: Reducing the equality to n mod pi lying in (0, pi/2) and checking twenty integers.
justification: One property-based reduction then a routine but careful check of twenty values; no insight beyond the principal ranges. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q8 (L2), piecewise tan^-1(tan x) counting.
